clue.text: One shows little authenticity in sound of instrument

indicators.note: 'sound of' asks for a word that is pronounced the same as the instrument named

parts.note: a lyre is a small harp of ancient Greece

explanation.surface: Someone with poor authenticity is caught up in the tone of an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in sound of' signals a word pronounced like LYRE: LIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tells untruths is hardly genuine, so a fibber shows little authenticity.

clue.text: Six-footer humming middle of sestet in key's first error

indicators.note: 'middle of' takes just the central pair of letters from the six-letter word sestet
'first' takes the opening letter of the word key's

parts.note: a bug is an error, especially in a computer program

explanation.surface: An insect buzzes while a poet's sestet carries a key error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humming' is British slang for smelling bad, which is why it belongs to the definition; the stink bug gives off a foul smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so a stink bug is a smelly six-footer.

clue.text: Horse around on instrument

indicators.note: 'around' places the horse's letters on either side of the word on

parts.note: GG, short for gee-gee, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A horse is trotting about near a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: GG, from gee-gee, is nursery talk for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gong is a metal disc struck as a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Instrument is Spooner's orchestral nightmare

indicators.note: Spooner's tells you to swap the opening sounds of the two words that follow

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, so orchestral hints at it
a nightmare situation is hell

explanation.surface: A musician calls an instrument their orchestral nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' swaps the starts of BAND HELL to give HAND BELL; 'orchestral nightmare' is a loose clue to band hell.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbell is a small bell rung by hand, often played in tuned sets.

clue.text: Speculator, denying role in collapse, causes trouble

indicators.note: 'denying' says the letters of role are refused and so removed from speculator
'in collapse' says what is left of the word falls into a new order

explanation.surface: A speculator, refusing a part, makes trouble during a market crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denying' takes R, O, L, E from SPECULATOR, leaving SPCUAT, and 'in collapse' rearranges it as ACTS UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave, which is causing trouble.

clue.text: They satisfy a burning need but their clients always arrive late

definitions.text: They satisfy a burning need but their clients always arrive late

parts.words: They satisfy a burning need but their clients always arrive late
parts.note: a burning need is literal cremation, and the clients are 'late' in the sense of deceased

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead, not tardy, and the burning is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crematoria are buildings where bodies of the dead are burned.

clue.text: Cutting-edge music, selling well with City hipsters at first

parts.note: a hit is a record that sells well
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: 'at first' takes only the opening letter of hipsters

explanation.surface: Hipsters in the City favour trendy music that is selling well.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech means using advanced technology, which is cutting-edge.

clue.text: Formerly connected with every other member's disappearance

indicators.note: losing every other letter of connected leaves its alternate letters, the members being its letters

explanation.surface: A man once linked to a club lost his membership when every other member vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every other member's disappearance' drops the odd letters of CONNECTED, leaving ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, a synonym of formerly.

clue.text: In refrain, trombone leads to start of music

indicators.note: 'In' says the answer sits inside the words that follow, across the comma

explanation.surface: A trombone leads off a refrain to open a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals that refraIN TROmbone holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a song or piece of music.

clue.text: Head of conservatoire appearing again on radio, playing instrument

indicators.note: 'playing' tells you the gathered letters are to be rearranged freely
'Head of' takes the first letter of conservatoire

parts.note: the head of conservatoire, C, appears a second time

explanation.surface: A conservatoire principal returns to the radio to play an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on radio' looks like a sounds-like cue but is anagram fodder; 'Head of' gives C, 'appearing again' gives it once more, and 'playing' rearranges CC ON RADIO.
explanation.definitionFit: The accordion is a bellows-driven keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Outlaws are sent legal IDs, lest these be discovered

indicators.note: 'these be discovered' says the outlaws' own letters are to be uncovered, scattered in order through the words before, the rest falling away

explanation.surface: Outlaws are given legal papers so they will not be found out.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are not consecutive: 'these be discovered' picks out aRE seNt lEGAl iDs lESt in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Renegades are those who have deserted a cause or broken with the law.

clue.text: Boatman's Boatman, you say? I don't agree!

parts.note: Boatman is the setter, so his own possession is 'my'

indicators.note: 'you say' asks for a word pronounced like the setter's pronoun for himself

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as 'I'

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a phrase about the setter's setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use their pseudonym for 'I' or 'me'; 'you say' gives EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: My eye! is an old exclamation of disbelief, a way to disagree.

clue.text: Liable to have start of music replacing run in trumpet

indicators.note: 'replacing ... in' swaps one letter of the trumpet word for another

parts.note: to trumpet is to blare loudly
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: 'start of' takes the first letter of music

explanation.surface: A trumpet is apt to have music's first note replace a run.
explanation.walkthrough: In BLARE, M takes the place of R.
explanation.definitionFit: To be liable is to be responsible for fault, which is being to blame.

clue.text: Boatman is into rock (a follower of Yes?) with this instrument

indicators.note: 'is into' says the sailor goes inside the rock

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill; Yes Tor is on Dartmoor, so tor follows Yes
AB, an able seaman, is a sailor or boatman

explanation.surface: The setter, a prog-rock fan of Yes, plays this instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes' looks like the rock band; it is Yes Tor, a Dartmoor hill. TOR is a rocky hill in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabor is a small drum, played with a pipe in folk music.

clue.text: Changes in speech implied stopping reparation

indicators.note: 'stopping' means the second piece plugs a gap within the first

parts.note: to make amends is to make reparation

indicators.note: 'in speech' asks for letters pronounced like the word for implied

parts.note: meant is a synonym of implied

explanation.surface: Changes in a speech hinted at halting war reparations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' looks like part of the surface's setting but is the sounds-like signal; 'stopping' puts that inside the reparation word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amendments are alterations made to a text, such as a law.

clue.text: Arrive on a higher note?

definitions.meaning: an informal way to say turn up or arrive
pitched up describes a raised musical note

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch up is slang for turning up, and literally raising a note's pitch.

clue.text: Originating perhaps overseas, like Kathak, as a dance

indicators.note: 'Originating' points to where each word begins, so take the initial letters

explanation.surface: A dance perhaps came from abroad, like the Kathak of India.
explanation.walkthrough: Kathak is a classical Indian dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively Bohemian dance in duple time.

clue.text: Get wrong note out with this instrument

indicators.note: 'out' says the note letter is dropped from the word for mishandle

parts.note: to bungle is to get something wrong

explanation.surface: A player hits a wrong note on this instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes N from BUNGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a valveless brass instrument used for military calls.

clue.text: Unfashionable dance music causing muscle contraction

indicators.note: 'Unfashionable' means removing the word for fashionable, in, from the music

parts.note: Latin is dance music from Latin America, such as salsa

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned dance music gives someone a cramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contraction' means an abbreviation, not a cramp: LAT is short for latissimus dorsi.
explanation.definitionFit: Lat is a shortened name for the latissimus dorsi, a broad back muscle.

clue.text: Diverting to marina, which is in Sicily

indicators.note: 'Diverting' means turning the letters off course into a new order

explanation.surface: A boat diverts to a marina on the Sicilian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diverting' rearranges TO MARINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Taormina is a hilltop resort town on the east coast of Sicily.

clue.text: Elgar composition for portable organ

indicators.note: 'composition' says the composer's letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: An Elgar piece is written for a small organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges ELGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A regal was a small portable reed organ of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Questioning start of gig, with band assumed sick

indicators.note: 'start of' takes the first letter of gig
'assumed' means the band takes on the sick letters within it

parts.note: a ring is a circular band
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Interviewers question a band about falling ill at the start of a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks musical but is a ring, the circular kind; 'assumed' means taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: A grilling is a hard interrogation, intense questioning.

clue.text: Get another instrument — there's a note missing

indicators.note: 'missing' says one letter has gone from the instrument's name

parts.note: a recorder is a woodwind instrument
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A musician buys a new instrument because a note is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes C out of RECORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder is to order a further supply, getting another.

clue.text: Ridiculous orange beast

indicators.note: 'Ridiculous' suggests nonsense, so the letters go into a silly new order

explanation.surface: An absurd orange-coloured animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ridiculous' rearranges ORANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is a wild ass of Asia, an animal.

clue.text: Three notes with bow out

parts.note: re, ti and re are three notes of the sol-fa scale, set side by side

explanation.surface: A violinist plays three notes with the bow, then exits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' suggests a violin; it belongs to the phrase bow out. Re, ti and re are sol-fa notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to withdraw from work or play, which is to bow out.

clue.text: Instrument's voice, even used with acoustic of large venue

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: 'even' takes the second and fourth letters of voice
'acoustic of' asks for letters pronounced like the venue word

parts.note: an arena is a large venue for sport or concerts

explanation.surface: An instrument's tone is enhanced by a big hall's acoustics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' gives OC from vOiCe; 'acoustic of' turns ARENA into ARINA.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument.

clue.text: Notes written here in Home Counties about tax return

indicators.note: 'about' places the region's letters around the tax

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE

indicators.note: 'return' means the tax word is read backwards

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: Someone files a tax return in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax return' reads as a form to file, but 'return' reverses the tax and 'about' wraps the region round it. The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: A stave is the set of five lines on which music notes are written.

clue.text: Instrument, but missing bag

indicators.note: 'missing' says the word but is left out of the instrument

parts.note: a sackbut is an early trombone

explanation.surface: An instrument has been left behind, but the bag is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' looks like a link word; it is removed from SACKBUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sack is a large coarse container for carrying goods, such as coal or potatoes.

clue.text: Look after work containing tangle of Mexican fruit

indicators.note: 'after' places the look word at the end
'containing' means the work word holds the tangle within it

parts.note: to toil is to work hard
a mat is a tangled mass, as of hair
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone tends a tangle of Mexican fruit plants at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as care for; 'after' instead puts LO behind TOMATIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomatillo is a small husked fruit used in Mexican salsas.

clue.text: Join up as part of orchestra

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to abut is to join at an edge

explanation.surface: Someone signs up to play in an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ABUT round.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the deepest brass instrument of an orchestra.

clue.text: Instrument of empty honour

indicators.note: 'of' here means made of, so the honour is built with nothing inside it

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
empty suggests nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: A medal is awarded hollow, as worthless as an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour; an empty one holds O.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Race with turns that are slippery

definitions.text: Race with turns that are slippery

indicators.note: 'that are slippery' says the letters slide out of place into a new order

explanation.surface: A race takes bends on a slippery surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that are slippery' rearranges RACE TURNS. The Cresta Run is an icy toboggan course at St Moritz.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cresta Run is a famous icy toboggan race track full of steep turns.

clue.text: How to use veto to get leader from jesting with this instrument?

parts.note: to use a veto is to ban something

indicators.note: 'to get ... from' says the leader is taken out of the jesting word

parts.note: joking means jesting
a king is a leader

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a veto might remove a joker from the instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman meant it as an instruction, BAN JO: banning JO from JOKING leaves KING, the leader. It reads equally as BAN plus JOKING with KING taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: The banjo is a stringed instrument with a drum-like body.
